# Todo

This file contains near term tasks with a short description
and reference links to more details.

Intro paragraphs in `## Todo` and `## Bugs` should begin every
line with 1 leading space so they don't match the `^\d+\. `
pattern that locates numbered entries; 2 or 3 spaces also work.

## In Progress

When a `## Todo` item is picked up, its text **moves** here
(never copied; one home per text). The picked-up task is a
`###` heading; a multi-cycle program adds one level, where the
program is the `###` and its current stage a `####` (headings
give the current work durable anchors, which numbered Todo
entries can't). The problem overview is followed by the
"plan", a bulleted list of the development "ladder". Each
rung is prepended with its commit reference, a literal
`[[N]]` placeholder until the commit is pushed, then
backfilled to a real file-local `[[n]]` ref (same pattern as
the chores As-built rungs):
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-0 blah (done)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-1 blah blah (current)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-2 blah blah blah
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y close-out and validation

### Refactor: typed jj facade -> jj-lib in-process; end subprocess spawning

Version-control operations were ~30 hand-rolled `run("jj", ...)`
spawns plus every mutation, with per-module private wrappers
and raw-git vestiges in init: stderr parsing instead of typed
errors, and jj's single-attempt index-lock acquisition (the
push `bookmark-set` lock race in [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md))
can't be retried where it fails. A multi-ladder program; the
staged plan, design detail, and the eight absorbed former
Todos live in
[refactor-20260716.md](notes/refactor-20260716.md).

Program ladder in **straight trunk order**, one bullet per
commit that lands on the branch, so reading it top to bottom
is reading `git log --first-parent`. `refactor:` entries are
the program's rungs, one per cycle (adjacent stages
consolidated 2026-07-24; titles are the anticipated close-out
titles; unshipped versions are provisional, since jj-lib may
split into two cycles). `docs:` entries are interludes that
sit between cycles and belong to no rung. Every shipped ref
points at a close-out commit published via the long-lived
`refactor-vc-x1` bookmark (merge-only while it ran; fully
merged into main and deleted 2026-08-03 under jj.md's
long-lived bookmark discipline).

The order is load-bearing: a
trapezoid's `<base>` is the parent of its own first rung, not
the previous close-out, so 0.78.0 bases on 0.77.4. Taking the
close-out instead swallows the interludes into the merge's
ladder side, which already bit at 0.76.0, whose base was the
0.75.1 interlude. See

## test: Claude Code can complete a cycle

- [[N]] 0.78.4 test: Claude Code can complete a cycle

`vc-x1 push` had been failing from sandboxed sessions, and the cause was never pinned down: the
failure always arrived at the end of a session, where the cheapest response was to hand the push
to wink and move on. The 2026-08-03 dogfood entry recorded the symptom and guessed at long-SSH
transfers. This cycle is the controlled experiment that settles it, run one step at a time so
each layer could be cleared separately, and the cycle is its own test: completing one end to end
from inside the sandbox is the result being demonstrated. It began as a throwaway on the
`cc-bm-and-push-test` bookmark and was promoted to a numbered cycle mid-run (wink, 2026-08-07)
once the finding proved worth keeping.

The cause, confirmed: both repos were originally cloned over ssh, and the sandbox denies ssh
twice over. Reads of `~/.ssh` are blocked except the commit-signing key and `known_hosts`, so no
auth key is available, and we think a host allowlist cannot admit a port-22 connection at all,
since ssh carries no SNI or Host header for a filter to match on. wink repointed both remotes at
https before the experiment, which is what made the push work.

- the network leg is a spawned `git`: `git_push_bookmark` hands
  `git_settings.to_subprocess_options()` to `jj_lib::git::push_refs`, so jj-lib runs the real
  `git` binary instead of doing the transfer in-process. That child inherits the sandbox, which
  is why a sandboxed run and wink's own terminal diverge on identical config
- credentials follow from that: git's own `store --file ~/.gitcreds` helper serves both repos,
  the sandbox permits reading it, and vc-x1 needs no credential callback of its own
- three competing hypotheses were killed by test rather than by argument. The bot repo is a real
  directory inside the project root, so it sits inside the write allowlist. The config paths the
  sandbox masks inside `.claude` are untracked, so no snapshot can record them as deleted. And
  jj's snapshot skips the character devices those masked paths become, without erroring
- the interactive-editor hypothesis died separately: `vc-x1 push` opens `$EDITOR` unless
  `--title`, `--body`, and `--yes` are all supplied, which would hang a non-interactive session,
  but wink confirmed the three-flag form works
- bugs.md #8's "sandboxed shell drops multi-MB pushes mid-transfer" is refined here rather than
  left standing: the size correlation was coincidence. Whether ssh fully explains that incident
  depends on iiac-perf's remotes having been ssh at the time, which this cycle did not check

One finding for the dogfood log: AGENTS.md places the bot repo at a symlink from
`~/.claude/projects/<path-to-project-root>/.claude`, which has one path component too many and
the direction reversed. `<project>/.claude` is the real directory, and the `projects` entry is
the symlink pointing in.

## Item 1, the ssh/https finding: already landed, nothing for the ladder

I checked before answering. It is recorded in three places, and well:

- `notes/chores/chores-16.md:202` -- the whole 0.78.4 section is the confirmed cause, including that the sandbox denies ssh twice over (no readable auth key, and we think a port-22 filter can't match without SNI), and the three competing hypotheses killed by test.
- `notes/dogfood.md:8` -- the 2026-08-07 entry, which explicitly corrects the 2026-08-03 guess about long SSH transfers.
- `notes/bugs.md:217` -- #8 refined, size correlation called coincidence.

So this needs no rung. Two loose ends remain and both are records, not code: the 0.78.4 As-built ref is still `[[N]]`, and 0.78.4 hasn't retired into `## Done`. Those ride whatever commits next.

The one thing genuinely unfinished is template-bound and can't be fixed here under hard rule 12: 0.78.4 found that AGENTS.md's bot-repo symlink path has a component too many and the direction reversed, and dogfood.md line 25 adds that an instruction set expecting a sandboxed agent should say to check its remotes. Both are pinned-file changes, so they want a mailbox message to `vc-x1-template` -- which is also where two unhandled messages already sit. Worth bundling into one reply rather than three trips.

## Item 2: I'd make it 0.80.0, not rungs inside 0.79.0

Your instinct about the *problem* is right and the diagnosis is sharper than Todo #2's. But I'd separate it from 0.79.0, for four reasons.

**The title has no room.** `refactor: trapezoid-push + body-intro validation` is 48 columns against custom.md's `<=50`. Hard rule 9 requires that exact string in the ladder rung, the chores `##` header, and the commit title. A third theme doesn't fit, and a cycle whose title can't name its contents is a cycle carrying too much.

**The ladder is open and `-0` has landed** on `trapezoid-push-vc-x1`. Amending it is mechanically cheap (TODO.md is edited every rung anyway, no re-describe involved), but it changes what the branch's trapezoid is measuring.

**The size is a full cycle.** Non-test, non-version-gate, the real inventory is ~20 sites: `sync.rs` 6, `push.rs` 3, `init.rs` 5, `repo_utils.rs` 3, `clone.rs` 1, `jj.rs` 2. Operation restore via jj-lib isn't a wrapper swap, and replacing `jj diff --stat` means composing a jj-lib diff summary. That's four or five rungs -- 0.79.0's own size.

**A trapezoid cycle is the worst place to add cargo.** `0.79.0-4` dogfoods `trapezoid-push` on its own close-out with the manual four-step recipe as fallback. If that goes sideways, you want the branch's diff to be about the push pipeline, not about a sync rewrite.

**But** the thing you're actually reacting to is real: 0.79.0 declares itself "the program's last rung" and harvests and deletes `notes/refactor-20260716.md` at close-out. Ship it as written and the program ends without delivering its banner goal. So make **0.80.0 the last rung** instead. The edits are small and all in the branch's TODO.md: 0.79.0's bullet stops claiming last, and the plan-file harvest plus the 0.72.0 version-gap re-homing move to 0.80.0's close-out. Todo #2's own process lesson -- a program states its acceptance check at open, and close-out runs it -- then gets honored rather than becoming a second post-mortem.

The alternative is to close the program at 0.79.0 and run `run` removal as a standalone `## Todo` cycle, the way 0.78.3 and 0.78.4 were. Cheaper, but the program's record has to say it fell short of its banner.

## Three things to settle before that becomes a ladder

**"Remove `run`" and "end subprocess spawning" are different goals, and the second isn't literally achievable.** 0.78.4's own finding is that the network leg spawns `git` from inside jj-lib: `git_push_bookmark` hands `git_settings.to_subprocess_options()` to `jj_lib::git::push_refs`. With `run` deleted, vc-x1 still spawns git on every push, one frame lower. # MESSAGES.md - the community's message protocol

How members of the vc-x1 dual-repo family leave word for each other. A member is a human or a
repo's agent; a repo with a live session is written only by its own agent, so messages to it
land here instead.

Members: wink, vc-x1, iiac-perf, zc-ring-x1.

The protocol:

- **Mailboxes** are per-member files: `messages/<member>.md` (e.g. `messages/vc-x1.md`).
- **Created on demand, deleted when empty**: a mailbox exists only while something is pending,
  so `ls messages/` shows the community's open traffic at a glance and an absent file is a
  free no-op.
- **Each message** is a dated `##` entry with the sender in the header and a "Done when" line,
  so the recipient knows what closes it.
- **The recipient deletes** a message once handled (jj history is the archive; mailboxes hold
  only open items).
- **Messages are thin pointers, not state**: durable coordination state lives in topical files
  (e.g. the registry in [agents-protocol/snapshots.md](agents-protocol/snapshots.md)); a
  message says "action needed, see <file>" rather than restating the details.
- **Polling**: each repo's `custom.md` carries an acquaint-time line to check its mailbox
  here. Humans check by habit; agents need it written into their instructions.

### Typeable punctuation only

Durable text uses punctuation that can be typed at a terminal. The prohibition is on
*authoring*, not presence: a file may legitimately hold a banned character it transcribed (see
below), so a byte scan is not the rule and a sweep needs the authored/transcribed judgment.
Banned from authoring: `—`, `–`, `…`, `→`. None can be entered without a compose key or a paste, so none can be grepped for, and an em
dash next to option syntax reads as another flag. Unlike the semicolon rule above this one is
absolute: they cost nothing to write and are paid on every read, so a soft rule accumulates
them.

`…` becomes `...` and `→` becomes `->`. The dashes have no single replacement, because an em
dash usually stands in for a structural decision that was not made. Make the decision:

- **A bullet's title and its body sharing a line** is a heading and a paragraph. Make the body
  sub-bullets.
- **A term and its definition** (`jj diff`, `<base>`, a flag) takes a colon, which keeps a
  glossary or a command list at one line per entry.
- **A prose aside** takes a comma, parentheses, or two sentences. Often the aside should just
  go.

Converting a heading moves its anchor. The em dash strips but the spaces on both sides survive,
so `## A — B` slugs to `#a--b` while its colon form slugs to `#a-b` (see
[Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links)). Re-point inbound links in the same
commit.

Scope is the same as [Speculation marker](#speculation-marker), plus commit titles and
everything under `src/`: doc comments, inline comments, and any user-visible string. Source is
the surface a human edits and greps most, so an untypeable character costs more there than in
prose. It applies going forward; existing text converts when touched. A code span is not exempt
by itself. Naming the character is a specimen and stays, which is how this section names them.
A banned character doing a job is a use and converts: `` `.expect(…)` `` becomes
`` `.expect(...)` ``.

Text quoted from outside this repo's prose (tool output, an error message, an already-published
commit title) is transcribed, not written, so it keeps its characters, whether or not it sits
in a code span. It matters most for commit titles: converting one stops it matching
`git log --grep` and breaks the verbatim identity that
[Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit) requires between
a commit title, its chores header, and its `## Done` entry.

### Conventional-commit shape (ladder / chores / commit)

A ladder step, its chores section, and its commit description share a *title* shape, a
[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) title (`<type>: <desc>`,
an optional `(scope)` after the type: `feat(push): ...`) over [Prose form](#prose-form) detail.
They differ in the title's prefix / marker (below) and in bullet *content*: commit bodies are
file-by-file, ladder / chores conceptual (see "Bullet *content* differs by surface" above). The
shared template:

```
<optional - X.Y.Z[-N]> <title>   # <title> is the commit's `<type>: <desc>`
<optional prose intro>
  - <optional item>
    <optional prose intro>
      - <optional sub-item>
      ...
```

The three surfaces apply it as:

- **Ladder step** (`TODO.md` `## In Progress`): the title is prefixed with the version
  (`X.Y.Z-N <title>`) and carries a `(current)` / `(done)` marker. The bare three-element
  `X.Y.Z` (no `-N`) is the close-out step. Detail is bulleted, never `;`-joined inline.
- **Chores section** (`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`): no version prefix, since the `##` header
  *is* the bare title, with the as-built ladder first under it (rungs open as `[[N]]`
  placeholders; see [Chores commit references](notes.md#chores-commit-references)).
- **Commit description**: no version prefix, and the title is the <=72-col first line; the body
  is the prose (file-by-file for the work repo, per
  [Per-commit flow](cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow)).

The title is **identical** across all three for a given step, so a step's ladder entry, its
chores `##` header, and its commit title line up verbatim; pick the commit title first and
reuse it.

That identity is **per step**, not per cycle: each step in a cycle gets its own distinct
descriptive title, never one shared cycle title uniquified by a step marker. The cycle's chores
section header carries the anticipated *close-out* title. To keep a cycle's commits collectable
with one `git log --grep`, give the step titles a common greppable stem (e.g. `config loader`).

**Cycle bookend titles**: the opening commit's title is the close-out title plus " opening",
same type (`feat: dynamic warmup opening` / `feat: dynamic warmup`), so one
`git log --grep "<close-out title>"` returns exactly the pair that brackets the cycle. The
type repeats the close-out's even though an opening is mostly bookkeeping: identical prefixes
make the pair scannable. Rungs between keep their own titles on the stem.

## Speculation marker

## 2026-08-07 from vc-x1 (o5) + wink: six items for the next agent-files configuration

wink says you are setting the next agent-files configuration now, for the
measure-reproducibility change. Six items, all new since our 2026-08-05 message, which stays
open on its own terms (revsets, the `.vc-config.toml` schema, the propose-a-pinned-change
mechanism); this one does not restate it. Items 1 and 2 are text you would otherwise carry
forward wrong, so they are the ones that want doing before the configuration lands.

**1. AGENTS.md's bot-repo symlink path is factually wrong.** The dual-repo section places the
bot repo at a "symlink from `~/.claude/projects/<path-to-project-root>/.claude`". That is one
path component too many and the direction reversed: `<project>/.claude` is the real directory,
and the entry under `~/.claude/projects/<path>/` is the symlink pointing in. Found at vc-x1's
0.78.4, 2026-08-07, and recorded in its dogfood log. It sits in the paragraph that introduces
the model, so it misleads on first read, and an agent that follows it looks in the wrong place
for the repo it is about to commit to.

**2. Nothing in the pinned set tells a sandboxed agent about ssh.** vc-x1's 0.78.4 was a
controlled experiment settling why `vc-x1 push` had failed from sandboxed sessions for weeks:
both repos were cloned over ssh, and a sandbox denies ssh twice over. Reads of `~/.ssh` are
blocked except the commit-signing key and `known_hosts`, so no auth key is available, and we
think a host allowlist cannot admit a port-22 connection at all, since ssh carries no SNI or
Host header for a filter to match on. Repointing both remotes at https is what made the push
work.

- the proposal: one line in the pinned set saying that a project whose agent runs sandboxed
  wants https remotes, and that an ssh remote is the first thing to check when a push dies at
  the network leg
- worth pinning because the cost of not having it was measured: three sessions handed their
  push to wink and moved on, and a 2026-08-03 dogfood entry recorded a wrong cause (the
  sandbox killing long ssh transfers, inferred from a size correlation that was coincidence)
- one item for your side: vc-x1 bugs.md #8's "sandboxed shell drops multi-MB pushes
  mid-transfer" came from your environment note. Whether ssh explains that incident too
  depends on your remotes having been ssh at the time, which 0.78.4 did not check. Worth a
  look, since if they were, that bug's remaining mystery dissolves

**3. The commit-description convention should land in the pinned files.** It is your text:
vc-x1 adopted problem-plus-solution as a custom.md override at 0.78.3 on 2026-08-06 and has
dogfooded it since. The proposal is to pin it, which retires our override.

- it touches cycle-protocol.md "Commit description", cycle-checklists.md step 7, prose.md's
  Conventional-commit shape, and notes.md's "the commit body is the mechanical record"
  doctrine, which becomes "the diff is"
- prose.md is the load-bearing edit and the easiest to miss: its "commit bodies are
  file-by-file" is the line that contradicts the convention. Configure the next set without it
  and the pinned file keeps asserting file-by-file bodies while both repos write
  problem-plus-solution ones
- our evidence, independent of yours: the 0.78.3 file-by-file body needed five redrafts across
  the cycle's riders, restating a diff already reviewed at the ready-to-commit gate

**4. A program should state its acceptance check at open, and its close-out should run it.**
For cycle-protocol.md's Close-out, proposed with evidence rather than as a suggestion. vc-x1's
jj-lib refactor program opened against "end subprocess spawning" and ran seven disciplined
cycles; 0.78.0's commit body claimed the goal met. About twenty spawn sites survived, two of
them inside the facade the program built, feeding stdout to a string parser: the exact pattern
the program had named. Found at the 0.78.3 review on 2026-08-06, after every cycle's own
checklist had passed. The per-commit and close-out checklists are per-cycle instruments, and
nothing in the pinned set checks a multi-cycle program against its own banner. vc-x1 is
repairing it with a rung added today, 0.80.0, that delivers the goal and states the check in
its header at open.

- relevant to what you are configuring for: a measurement change is exactly the shape that
  wants this, since "we measured it" is easy to believe and hard to notice you have not done

**5. `## Done` entries should carry the version** (wink, 2026-08-03; not previously sent).
Looking for 0.78.2 in `## Done` found nothing. notes.md's "Headings and entries that record a
commit" specifies title plus ref and no version, while the chores as-built rung two sections
later is `- [[1]] 0.78.2 style: ...`. Three records of one commit in three forms. The proposal
is to give Done the rung's form, `- 0.78.2 style: ... [[24]]: <prose>`. It does not collide
with the no-version rule, which bans a trailing `(<version>)`.

**6. A question, not a proposal: should hard rule 9 cover body shape?** It pins title identity
across the three surfaces today. The argument for extending it: a pushed body is
coordinate-first to fix under the re-describe rule, so a body-shape violation outlives the
review that missed it, which is the stated criterion for a hard rule. The argument against: the
hard-rules list earns its weight by staying short. We have no position. wink raised it, and it
wants a second opinion before it becomes text.

Done when: items 1 and 2 are in the payload before the next configuration lands, item 3 has a
verdict, and items 4, 5, and 6 have decisions or an explicit defer. None of it blocks the
measure-reproducibility work; items 1 and 2 only get more expensive once it starts.
